land.causeway.description: Raised paved causeway for one cell (3 m wide deck running north-south): a battered stone body, worn path paving on top and kerb stones along both edges; steps = a short flight down to the ground at the south end; end = a rounded terminus; broken = a collapsed middle with fallen slabs. Edge sockets on the north and south cell edges (origin on the cell centre at the datum; the steps run out past the south edge).

land.cliff.description: Mesa cliff on cell edges: a strata-banded face (cliff role) with jittered ledges, eroded buttresses and a sand cap on top; straight = a run along one edge, corner = an outer corner, end = a tapering spur, pillar = a free mesa butte. Closed solid; the face stands on its cell edge facing south (origin on the edge line at the datum; the rock runs 3 m back to the north).

land.ground.description: Ground tile on the RUIN GRID (cells x 4 m square, open sheet facing up): sand = soft dune ripples (sand role); jungle = earth and moss patches with hummocks (dirt role); paved = worn flagstones (path role); court = flat paving (path role). Edges lie exactly on the ground datum so tiles interlock edge to edge.

land.sky.description: Sky backdrop set: inward-facing dome (kit_shell_sky, role 'sky': the pack's painted deep zenith, pale horizon haze = fog colour, and the sun) plus an optional ring of distant silhouettes in the vista_far role (flat-topped mesas, rolling dunes or a jungle canopy line) just inside the dome. Origin at the viewer; bound as `sky.backdrop`.

land.skyline.description: Distant skyline card for the far band (vista_far role, so it takes the pack's horizon haze and most of the distance fog): one flat silhouette facing south. city = an original temple-city outline (stepped pyramids, a pylon pair, obelisk spikes, broken colonnade stumps); mesas = flat-topped buttes; canopy = rounded jungle crowns with a stepped pyramid top breaking through. Place 50-120 m out; its foot sinks 1 m below the datum.

land.slope.description: Slope between terrace levels inside one cell run (4 m long, width_cells x 4 m wide): a soft S-curved sand or earth ramp climbing north with cliff-role flanks. Sockets at the foot (ground datum) and the crest (at the rise).

land.terrace.description: Raised terrace / plateau block for tiered terrain: a flat top (sand or earth-and-moss) on battered, eroded cliff-role sides, cells x 4 m at the top so a land.slope crest or a stair flight meets its edge on the grid. Closed solid; the foot spreads `batter` m past the cell block and sinks below the datum. Sockets 'terrace_edge' on the four top edges.

land.wash.description: Dry wash / stream-bed ground tile: a cells x 4 m ground sheet with a meandering sunken channel running north-south (the channel re-centres on the tile's north and south edges so washes chain tile to tile) and a scatter of rounded pebbles in its bed. Outside the channel the edges lie on the ground datum like land.ground. Sockets 'wash' where the channel crosses the north and south edges, 'ground_edge' on east and west.

relic.altar.description: Altar: stepped base, a dressed block with a carved procession relief on its front and a moulded top. basin = glazed offering bowl; sun = gold sun disc on a stand (the shrine focus); fire = a fire bowl (runtime emitter).

relic.banner.description: Woven banner on a wall bracket (wall-mounted, origin on the wall face): a crossbar with gold finials and a hanging cloth with a woven border and an original rayed-sun emblem (fabric role, two-sided).

relic.brazier.description: Brazier: gold-leaf bowl on a bronze tripod, on a carved stone pedestal, or a low stone fire pit; a lit flame (emissive) and a runtime warm emitter (meta.emitter, mirrored in view.json look.emitters). unlit = cold tripod.

relic.coffer.description: Reliquary coffer (the goal object): a carved stone casket on four squat feet with gold corner caps and a lid carrying the sun inlay; open = lid tipped back on its hinge showing the dark inside.

relic.dial.description: Sun-dial puzzle dais: a round stepped platform, a ring of tapered ray stones and a central gnomon with a gold tip; ruined = two rays toppled and a cracked step. Socket 'puzzle' at the gnomon.

relic.plate.description: Pressure-plate floor tile (1.2 m): a sunk stone frame and a plate carrying the sun inlay (frame role) or a glyph (hull role); raised = 8 cm proud, pressed = flush. Socket 'plate' at the centre (triggers stay in game data).

relic.sarcophagus.description: Sarcophagus: a stone chest with incised glyph bands along both sides on a plinth, and a battered lid carved with the sun-wheel relief; open = lid slid aside showing the dark interior; broken = lid cracked in two on the floor.

relic.statue.description: Statue of an ORIGINAL invented figure: keeper = robed standing figure holding a gold sun disc under a fan crown of three fins, with a back pillar, on a stepped plinth (3.4 m); guardian = seated crested beast (plate crest, curled tail, gold collar disc) on a long plinth; buried = the colossal keeper head sunk to the chin in a sand mound with one fallen crown fin; idol = a small seated gold figure with a rayed disc head on a carved pedestal.

relic.tablet.description: Glyph stone: stele = round-topped standing slab with an incised glyph face (original glyph grammar, hull role) on a base; tablet = a low inclined tablet on a stand (paper role glyphs); fallen = a stele broken in two in the sand; awakened = stele whose glyphs glow (emissive screen role + a cool runtime emitter).

relic.urn.description: Painted clay urn (terracotta with painted bands and a zigzag frieze; glazed bowl): jar, two-handled amphora, wide bowl, or a broken jar with a jagged rim and a shard.

ruin.arch.description: Freestanding arch: two chamfered piers with moulded bases; round = voussoir ring with a carved keystone; corbel = stepped corbel vault outline; broken = one pier and a fallen half-ring among blocks.

ruin.column.description: Temple column (original order): stepped square plinth, rounded base ring, faceted shaft with entasis and two carved limestone rings, a flared 'sun cup' capital under a square abacus. broken = snapped shaft with a fallen drum; stump = plinth and a jagged metre of shaft; fallen = drums and capital lying in the sand.

ruin.court.description: Sunken court: stepped stone terraces rising outward around a court floor at y = 0 (the player's floor), swept as one closed stepped profile with mitred corners; open sides leave a 4 m entrance gap centred on that side (door sockets there).

ruin.floor.description: Paving slab for one RUIN GRID cell (4 x 4 m, 5 cm proud of the ground, chamfered) on a joint bed that fills the joints with sand/moss: plain; cracked = broken slabs with sand between; inlay = central sun inlay (frame role); block = 2 x 2 cells; ceiling = coffered slab hung at the storey height facing down (origin stays on the floor datum).

ruin.gate.description: Temple gate on the door anchor (room.gd places 'arch.door' 0.4 m in from the room edge; this frame covers the 2.8 x 3.6 m wall cut): doorway = carved jambs and lintel with a sun-inlay keystone (the frame bound to arch.door); sealed = the same frame closed by a carved stone slab (state swap); pylon = a monumental gate of two battered towers and a carved beam around the standard frame (spans 3 cells).

ruin.obelisk.description: Obelisk: tapered square shaft on a two-step base, glyph panels (original glyph grammar, hull role) on all four faces and a sphere-mapped gold cap. broken = snapped shaft with the top lying beside it; short = waist-high waystone.

ruin.pier.description: Corner pier on a cell corner: chamfered square shaft on a moulded base with a stepped capital; hides the joint where two walls meet. broken = ragged snapped top; low = parapet post.

ruin.pyramid.description: Stepped pyramid: battered tiers with a dressed lip, an optional stair flight up the south face with sloped balustrades, and an optional summit shrine (doorway house under a stepped roof) or altar. tiers = 1 is a single walkable tier block.

ruin.rampart.description: Rampart on a cell edge: battered outer face, a 2 m walk on top and a crenellated parapet (tapered merlons); corner = L-shaped quarter; tower = round bastion; broken = a breach with spilled blocks.

ruin.rubble.description: Collapsed rubble: tumbled dressed blocks and broken stone (small, large pile), blocks half-buried in a drifted sand mound (drift), or a heap of column drums.

ruin.stairs.description: Monumental stair flight inside one cell: 0.25 m risers climbing north (glTF -Z) with sloped balustrades ending in disc terminals; ruined = missing treads and a cracked balustrade. Sockets: stair_bottom (south edge) and stair_top (north edge, at the rise).

ruin.wall.description: Carved sandstone wall segment on a cell edge: a closed 1 m solid centred on the boundary (inner faces 0.5 m in), plinth, dressed cornice; door = 2.8 x 3.6 m cut with a lintel (the standard frame covers it), window = slit, relief = carved panel on both faces, broken = ragged collapsed top with fallen blocks, low = parapet.

wild.dune.description: Sand dune: a soft mound, a crescent dune with a steep slip face on its lee (north) side, or a long wind ridge; closed solid sunk 0.2 m below the ground datum so its foot meets any ground tile.

wild.fern.description: Fern: a rosette of arching two-sided fronds (fan) or a tall upright spray, rooted in a small leaf-litter mound.

wild.log.description: Jungle deadwood: a fallen mossy log with a broken end, a tangle of arching surface roots, or a hollow stump.

wild.oasis.description: Oasis pool (the lane's own water piece): a water disc at WATER_Z = -0.25 m (water role, slow UV scroll, no wobble) inside a closed bank ring that slopes from the ground datum into the water, with a reed bed and lily pads, on a square ground skirt that fills its cell block (cells x 4 m) at the datum, so it drops into a gap in the ground tiles and meets them edge to edge (ground_edge sockets). jungle = an earth-and-moss bank and darker water. Sockets 'shore' on the bank, 'water' at the surface.

wild.palm.description: Date palm: a gently curved trunk of chevron leaf-base scales tapering to a crown of V-folded two-sided fronds with a date cluster; leaning = strong lean (oasis edge); young = short with a low crown; twin = two trunks from one root. Origin at the trunk base.

wild.reeds.description: Reeds and grasses: a tuft of blades, tall umbel-topped water reeds (papyrus-like heads, two-sided) or a low dry grass clump; two-sided blades. Origin at the root.

wild.rock.description: Rocks: a weathered boulder, a cluster of three, a wind-carved pillar rock (stacked strata lumps with a cap) or a tilted slab outcrop.

wild.shrub.description: Shrub: a desert scrub of low leaf masses on dry stems, a jungle broadleaf clump of big drooping two-sided leaves, or a flowering bush (foliage masses dotted with blossom clusters).

wild.tree.description: Jungle tree: a straight trunk on four buttress roots under a crown of rounded leaf clumps (a high dome over three lower clumps) with a few hanging vines; tall = slimmer, higher crown; strangler = roots and trunk wrapped around a broken stone column. Origin at the trunk base.

wild.vines.description: Hanging vine curtain for a wall top (wall-mounted, origin on the wall face at floor level): leafy strands of uneven length draped from the top edge and a mossy leaf roll along the coping.

note: Every GLB here exists for consumers only with this sha256 (explicit sRGB8, converted after the kit validators and the ANCIENTKIT gates ran on the linear build; source_sha256 = validated build). textures are relative to kits/library/.
